rows.notes: The paper is explicitly a review summarising KSU studies published elsewhere (Lamm et al. 1995a water requirement and yields, Fig. 2-3 'data from Lamm et al. 1995a'; Caldwell et al. 1994 frequency; Lamm et al. 1997a and Manges et al. 1995 dripline spacing; Lamm et al. 1997b N fertigation, Fig. 4; O'Brien et al. 1998 economics, Fig. 5 'adapted from'). The only apparently original data are the 10-year zone flow-rate monitoring records (Fig. 6, system life), which bear on system longevity rather than directly on corn yield or profitability. Because the yield (12.5-13.4 Mg/ha with ~25% less net irrigation) and profitability (SDI competitive with center pivot for fields smaller than ~50 ha if system life 10-20 years) results supporting the claim are all drawn from previously published primary studies, the paper is rated as a review (Q1 no). Direction of the claim is consistent with what the review summarises for Kansas silt loam soils; the Texas High Plains part of the claim comes from Howell et al. (1997), which this paper only cites.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Self-described review of 10 years of Kansas SDI corn research by the authors' own group; figures reproduce data from earlier primary publications, except Fig. 6 (long-term flow-rate uniformity of 23 zones, 1989-1998) which appears to be newly reported monitoring data on system life.
